post.description:
Initialize a new image.\
\
Prepares the database-entry and the onsen, before the files are uploaded. Sakura uses this to\
store the root-disk of a virtual_machine as snapshot, which is marked by `is_snapshot`. The image\
starts with the status `ENCRYPTING` and can not be used, until sakura sets it to `READY`. With\
`secret_uuid`, the image is encrypted with this already existing secret of the omamori, instead of\
a new generated secret.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

Get information of an image from the database.

put.description:
Set the status of an image, optionally together with type and size of its\
file.\
\
Sakura uses this for snapshots, which are registered before their file exists: the status is set to\
`UPLOADING` together with type and size of the file, before the encrypted file is uploaded into the\
onsen, and to `READY`, when the snapshot is complete. Type and size are measured on the unencrypted\
file and have to be provided together.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

get.description: List basic information of all images from the database.

post.description:
Create new image by uploading a multipart-form with the fields `name`,\
`image_type` (at the moment only `disk`), the optional `secret_uuid` and the disk-image as `file`.\
With `secret_uuid`, the image is encrypted with this already existing secret of the omamori,\
instead of a new generated secret.\
\
The image is registered with the status `ENCRYPTING`, when the file is completely uploaded, while\
ryokan encrypts the file. While the encrypted file is stored in the onsen, the status is\
`UPLOADING`. Afterwards the image is `READY` and can be used for virtual machines. If the encryption\
or the storing fails, the image is removed again.\
\
Before the file is encrypted, its type (e.g. `qcow2` or `raw`) is identified and its size is\
measured. Both are returned as `file_type` and `file_size`.

This is called by the onsen-host itself without user-interaction, so it requires\
no token, but is protected by the internal api-key and the registration-key.

put.description:
Set, if an onsen-host is a backup-target.\
\
A backup-target only stores backups and is never used for normal images or snapshots. A host can\
only be marked as backup-target, while no images or snapshots are stored on it, and the mark can\
only be removed, while no backups are stored on it anymore. This can only be done by an admin.

post.description:
Create a new backup, whose package is stored as one directory\
`backups/<uuid>` on a backup-target.\
\
The backup starts in the state `CREATING`, in which files can be written into the package. With\
`host_uuid` the package is stored on this backup-target, otherwise ryokan selects one. Users, which\
are not admin, can only create backups of their own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

post.description:
Register a package, which was copied onto a backup-target from outside, for\
example from another deployment, as backup.\
\
The package must be in `backups/<uuid>` on the backup-target and contain a manifest. Like with\
finalizing a backup, the number and size of all files and the sha256 of the manifest are read from\
the backup-target, and the backup is directly registered as sealed package in the state `READY`.\
This can only be done by an admin.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

get.description:
Read a file, like the metadata or the manifest, from the package of a backup.\
\
Files can only be read, after the package was finalized and is in the state `READY`. The\
query-parameter `path` is relative to the directory of the package. The file is returned\
base64-encoded and can have at most 16 MiB.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: path of the file relative to the directory of the package

schema.description: path of the file relative to the directory of the package

put.description:
Write a file, like the metadata or the manifest, into the package of a\
backup. An existing file with the same path is overwritten.\
\
Files can only be written, while the backup is in the state `CREATING`. The `path` is relative to\
the directory of the package and the base64-decoded `content` can have at most 16 MiB.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

get.summary: Get info of file in backup
get.description:
Get the size and the sha256 of a file within the package of a backup.\
\
It is used to write the checksums of all files into the manifest, before the package is\
finalized, and to check them again, before a backup is restored. So it is allowed in the states\
`CREATING` and `READY`. The query-parameter `path` is relative to the directory of the package.\
Large files, like the disks, take their time, because their whole content is read by the onsen.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: path of the file relative to the directory of the package

schema.description: path of the file relative to the directory of the package

post.description:
Copy a file between the package of a backup and the normal onsens.\
\
The file is streamed chunk by chunk from the source-onsen to the target-onsen, without storing it in\
ryokan. If the copy fails, the incomplete copy is deleted again.\
\
- `INTO_BACKUP`: the file of the `READY` image `image_uuid` is copied unchanged into the package\
  under `path`. The package must be in the state `CREATING`.\
- `OUT_OF_BACKUP`: the file `path` of the package is copied to a normal onsen under\
  `images/<image_uuid>`, where it can be registered as image with this UUID afterwards. The UUID\
  must not be used by any image yet and the package must be in the state `READY`, so it stays\
  untouched.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

Get the target, where the root-disk of a virtual_machine is uploaded into the\
package of a backup.\
\
The disk is uploaded directly into the onsen of the backup-target, so only its address and the path\
of the disk are returned. The disk is no image, so it is not registered as image. This is only\
possible, while the backup is in the state `CREATING`.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

get.description:
Get the state of the package of a backup together with the backup-target,\
which stores it.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

delete.description:
Delete a backup together with its whole package on the backup-target.\
\
The package is only deleted as a whole and can be deleted in every state. It gets the state\
`DELETING` first, so it can't be read anymore. If the deletion of the files fails, the backup stays\
in this state and the deletion can be repeated.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

post.description:
Seal the package of a backup, after all files were written into it.\
\
The number and size of all files and the sha256 of the manifest are read from the backup-target\
and stored together with the state `READY`. From now on the package is read only. A package\
without `manifest.json` is incomplete, so it gets the state `ERROR` and can only be deleted.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

get.description:
List the packages on a backup-target, which are not registered as backup.\
\
These are packages, which were copied onto the backup-target from outside, for example from another\
deployment. Only directories in `backups/`, whose name is a UUID, are listed. `has_manifest` shows,\
if the package is complete and can be registered. This can only be done by an admin.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

Read the manifest of a package on a backup-target, which is not registered as\
backup yet, like a package, which was copied from another deployment.\
\
The manifest describes, to which project the package belongs, so it is read before the package is\
registered. Only packages, which are found by the scan of the backup-target, can be read. The\
manifest is returned base64-encoded. This can only be done by an admin.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

parameters.name: backup_uuid
parameters.description: UUID of the package, which is the name of its directory on the backup-target

schema.description: UUID of the package, which is the name of its directory on the backup-target

get.description: Count the images of a project, which still exist. It is used by miko to check, if a project is empty, before it is deleted. This can only be done by an admin.

Export the images and snapshots of a project for a backup.\
\
Only the metadata is exported. The files are copied into the backup separately and their location\
is not part of the export. Images, which are not `READY`, are skipped, because their file is not\
complete. Backups are not part of the export. Users, which are not admin, can only export their\
own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

post.description:
Import the images and snapshots of a project from a backup.\
\
The files of the images must already be copied to a normal onsen, for example with\
`POST /v1alpha/backup/{backup_uuid}/copy/internal`. Each image is registered as `READY` with the\
location of its copy (`onsen_address` and `file_path` within `images/`). A backup-target or an\
unknown onsen is rejected with `400`.\
\
The images keep their UUIDs, unless the `id_map` gives them a new one, which is also applied to\
their secrets. A UUID, which is used by another project, is rejected with `409`. An existing\
image of the project with the same UUID is rejected with `409`, unless `force` is set, which\
overwrites it and deletes its old file, if the location changed. All conflicts are checked, before\
anything is changed. The quota of the project is not checked here.\
Users, which are not admin, can only import into their own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

Secret.description:
Wrapper around a string, which must not be leaked into logs or error-messages.

`Debug` and `Display` both print `***` instead of the content, so a secret stays hidden even when it is part of a bigger struct, which is logged as a whole. The content is only reachable through `reveal`, which makes every intended access visible at the call-site.
